not_seedable.mechanism: detector `port-binding-report` -- RD-02, and it was a detector that could not run
not_seedable.reason:
ITS ENTRY POINT STOPPED ACCEPTING ITS OWN ARGV WHEN SM-02 LANDED, AND NOTHING
NOTICED FOR TWO EPICS. The column passed `--port-manifest` to
`run_generated_case_adapters.py`; SM-02 deleted that flag with the rest of the
`[ports.*]` machinery. Since then the detector exits 2 with `unrecognized
arguments`, executes nothing, and the runner reports `INERT` -- which decides
nothing and is correctly not a survival, so the table was never WRONG. It was
carrying a column that could never say anything again, in a file whose whole
argument is that a control which cannot fail is worse than no control (R2).

Measured, not asserted. At `7514df0`, `SM-GM-P2` against this column:
`INERT`, `executed = 0`, `exit = 2`, while `pytest-full` killed the same mutant
at 1426 executed nodes. The gap this removal opens is therefore the gap the
column was already failing to cover, and `pytest-full` covers it -- re-measured
after the cut in
`specs/results/scorecards/reading-discipline/GOAL-apparatus-priced/`.

Named here rather than deleted silently, because a detector that vanishes from
a table is how a denominator shrinks (`denominator_rule`).

IT CORRECTLY CANNOT FAIL. It is a thermometer: it reports, refuses nothing,
gates nothing, and `EXIT_OK = 0` is the only exit constant in the file. There is
no gap to seed because there is no claim to catch anything. Named here so that
its absence from the mutant table is a decision on the record rather than an
omission, and so that SM-03 does not cut it by counting it with the other eight
that cannot be shown to fail.
not_seedable.removed_by: nothing; it is NOT a removal target

not_seedable.reason:
NOT IN THIS ENVIRONMENT. Running the Test Graph nodes needs gradle, a JVM and
JBang, none of which are available here. A mutant seeded into them would report
INERT on every detector, and an INERT row would be indistinguishable from a
survival to any reader skimming the table. Declared unmeasured rather than
measured as nothing.

not_seedable.mechanism: the `fake =` key of a `[ports.*]` table itself
not_seedable.reason:
THE FAULT WOULD LIVE IN THE MECHANISM'S OWN DECLARATION. Dropping `fake =` from
`case_adapters.port-swap.toml` is caught today by `render_oracle_statement`
('is bound as a port and declares no fake'). But the table is deleted with the
machinery, so there is no post-removal tree the mutant could be re-applied to,
and a before-only reading decides nothing about the cut. SM-GM-P2 seeds the
equivalent drift in the MANIFEST instead, which outlives SM-02 and is therefore
re-runnable. Reported so the difference is a decision, not an oversight.

THE GAP IS ALREADY TOTAL AND THERE IS NOWHERE TO SEED IT. The row is classified
`no-instrument-exists`: `ticket.yaml`'s `status` is written once by the
scaffolder and read by nothing (`PA-02-DF-02`, open). Every `ticket.yaml` in the
tree is under `specs/.history`, which is append-only and must not be mutated
even in a copy. The cost of removing this row is therefore already paid in full
and no mutant is needed to price it -- but it is named, because a row that
vanishes silently from a removal table is how a denominator shrinks.

SM-GM-P2-manifest-renames-the-port-out-f.claims_to_catch: a port renamed in the manifest while the mapping still binds the old name -- the only executable reconciliation between a `[ports.*]` table and `spec_manifest.yaml`
SM-GM-P2-manifest-renames-the-port-out-f.gap:
DRIFT BETWEEN THE DECLARATION AND THE BINDING. `render_port_binding_report` is
the one thing in the toolchain that compares the two directions and says
`BOUND BUT NOT DECLARED` / `DECLARED BUT NOT BOUND`. It is removed with the
machinery. The fault seeded here is in the MANIFEST -- a shipped model
artifact that outlives SM-02 -- so the mutant is still re-runnable after the
cut, which a mutant seeded inside the mapping table would not be.
